2b.comment: -0.5 S7 vA is undefined because v has 1 column and A has 3 rows, and matrix multiplication is not commutative, so Av written sideways is not vA.

2c.comment: -0.5 E5 Aw is called undefined with no dimension reason, which must state that A has 3 columns and w has 1 row.

3a.comment: -1 E2 Row operations are not labeled, so write R2 → R2 - 2R1 beside each step the way you did in (b).

4c.comment: -1 E2 Row operations are not labeled, so label every step, starting with R1 → R1 - 2R3.

5a.comment: -1 E8 Arithmetic slip in R2 → R2 - 2R1, whose second entry is 4 - 2(2) = 0, so that row is [0 0 1] and the RREF is [1 2 0; 0 0 1; 0 0 0], not I.

5b.comment: -1 S3 The slip in (a) changed the conclusion, since the correct RREF has pivots only in columns 1 and 3, so rank(A) = 2, not 3.

5c.comment: -2 S7 Exactly one solution is impossible because column 2 is never a pivot column, so x2 is free whenever the system is consistent, and claiming uniqueness earns 0 for that piece; -2 S3 Zero solutions is possible when b3 ≠ b1 + b2 and infinitely many is possible when b3 = b1 + b2, so both cases you ruled out are lost.

deductions.comment: vA is undefined because v has 1 column and A has 3 rows, and matrix multiplication is not commutative, so Av written sideways is not vA.
Aw is called undefined with no dimension reason, which must state that A has 3 columns and w has 1 row.
Row operations are not labeled, so write R2 → R2 - 2R1 beside each step the way you did in (b).
Row operations are not labeled, so label every step, starting with R1 → R1 - 2R3.
Arithmetic slip in R2 → R2 - 2R1, whose second entry is 4 - 2(2) = 0, so that row is [0 0 1] and the RREF is [1 2 0; 0 0 1; 0 0 0], not I.
The slip in (a) changed the conclusion, since the correct RREF has pivots only in columns 1 and 3, so rank(A) = 2, not 3.
Exactly one solution is impossible because column 2 is never a pivot column, so x2 is free whenever the system is consistent, and claiming uniqueness earns 0 for that piece.
Zero solutions is possible when b3 ≠ b1 + b2 and infinitely many is possible when b3 = b1 + b2, so both cases you ruled out are lost.

overall_comment: Label every row operation: 3(a) and 4(c) carry none, and that costs a point each. Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so vA is undefined rather than Av on its side. Problem 5 turns on one entry: R2 → R2 - 2R1 gives [0 0 1], and carrying [0 1 1] forward produced rank 3 and a unique solution for every b, which reverses all three cases in (c).
